question_text: Your teammate is struggling to finish an important task before the deadline. What would you most likely do?
option_a: Drop your own work and help them finish it.
option_b: Tell your manager straight away so they can re-plan.
option_c: Stay focused on your own deliverables.
option_d: Work through it with them so they can finish it themselves.

question_text: You realise halfway through the day that you may not finish your own work before the deadline. What would you most likely do?
option_a: Tell the team immediately and ask for suggestions.
option_b: Keep working alone and only ask for help if it becomes unavoidable.
option_c: Re-prioritise and finish the most critical parts first.
option_d: Stay late as long as it takes to finish everything yourself.

question_text: You spot a mistake in work your team already delivered to the client. Nobody else has noticed. What do you do?
option_a: Raise it immediately, even though it reflects badly on the team.
option_b: Fix it quietly and say nothing.
option_c: Mention it to your manager privately first.
option_d: Wait and see whether the client notices.

question_text: A colleague asks you to sign off on work you have not actually reviewed. What do you do?
option_a: Sign it. You trust them and the deadline is tight.
option_b: Review it properly first, even if that misses the deadline.
option_c: Sign it but note that you did not review it.
option_d: Ask someone else to review it in your place.

question_text: Three weeks into a project your team's approach clearly is not working. What do you do?
option_a: Propose a different approach and make the case for it.
option_b: Raise your concerns and let the team decide.
option_c: Keep going. Changing direction now would waste the work already done.
option_d: Quietly start building an alternative in parallel.

question_text: A major release fails in production an hour before you were due to finish. How do you react?
option_a: Take charge of the response and coordinate the fix.
option_b: Work steadily through the problem without getting rattled.
option_c: Escalate to whoever is on call and hand it over.
option_d: Push through, but find it hard to think clearly.

question_text: Which of these is more true of you?
option_a: I am the person who keeps everyone aligned.
option_b: I am the person who quietly gets things finished.

question_text: Which matters more to you at work?

option_a: I adapt quickly when priorities change.
option_b: I hold a plan steady once it has been agreed.

question_text: The deadline is tight. Which would you prefer?
option_a: Deliver quickly, accepting a few minor mistakes.
option_b: Take the extra time to make sure everything is right.

question_text: A decision needs making and the team is split. Which would you prefer?
option_a: Make the call yourself and move on.
option_b: Check with the team before deciding.

question_text: Something has gone wrong on your work. Which would you prefer?
option_a: Escalate it early, even if it turns out to be nothing.
option_b: Solve it yourself and report once it is resolved.

question_text: You are starting something unfamiliar. Which would you prefer?
option_a: Plan the work out thoroughly before starting.
option_b: Start, and adjust as you learn.

option_d: Backing a decision before all the data is in
